title: Apply environment overrides to default settings
examObjective: Predicting the result of core DataWeave functions
basics: `++` on two Objects does not replace fields; it appends the pairs of the right Object after those of the left, so a key present in both appears twice. Many JSON parsers then quietly keep only one of them, which hides the problem.
prompt:
A service reads `{ defaults, overrides }`. Every override is for a setting that exists in `defaults`. Return the effective settings: every default, with its value replaced where an override exists, keeping the defaults' key order.

An override may set a setting to `false` or `0`, and that override must win.

The output is compared exactly as text, so each setting must appear once.
hints: Try `payload.defaults ++ payload.overrides` on the second hidden case and read the output as text.
Walk the defaults, and for each key take the override if there is one.
`payload.defaults mapObject ((v, k) -> { (k): payload.overrides[k] default v })`. `default` keeps `false` and `0`.
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload.defaults mapObject ((v, k) -> { (k): payload.overrides[k] default v })

mustFail.why: concatenates the objects, so an overridden setting appears twice
tests the override for truthiness, so an override of false is ignored
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload.defaults mapObject ((v, k) -> { (k): if (payload.overrides[k] != null and payload.overrides[k] != false) payload.overrides[k] else v })

explanation.approach: `++` is concatenation, not merging: both `retries` keys survive, and the output depends on which one the consumer reads. Walking the defaults and looking each key up in the overrides writes every key exactly once, in the defaults' order. `default` replaces only null, so an override of `false` or `0` wins as it should.

snippets.label: Concatenation keeps both
snippets.note: Two keys with the same name.
